decisions.issues: v02 fixes the v01 fault: the headland building is gone, leaving only palms, scrub and rock. Nagoji matches his sheet: rust-red turban, red sash, thick moustache, clean-shaven chin. He stands in the stirrups with his arm flung out, shouting. His is the only grey horse. The Madurai lancers wear white turbans and ride dark bay and black horses. The Maravar riders are bare-headed on dun and brown ponies, and the line bows. The fishermen are bare-chested in plain white lungis and one is doubled over laughing. The whole upper right is open sky, with room for both captions. Minor notes: the laughing fisherman has no visible shoulder cloth; the lancers wear crossed straps, which the continuity row does not forbid; his ear ornament is hidden. v01 is not acceptable because of the building on the headland.

v02 fixes the v01 faults: the fisherman's lungi is now plain white (it was checked in v01), both men sit cross-legged on a palm-leaf mat with no table, and Nagoji's chin is clean. His eyes are watering and he grins with his mouth open and tongue out. There is no red on his lips or fingers, and the curry stays on the leaf. The lamp is an open clay lamp, and there is a coconut-shell cup of toddy. The fisherman is bare-chested with a cloth over one shoulder. A plain hut wall at upper centre (x 0.38 to 0.75, y 0.04 to 0.30) gives clean space for the caption. Deviation noted but not rejected: he fans with his LEFT hand, not the RIGHT the note asks for. The sleeve is pushed back and the back of the forearm faces the camera, so the inner forearm and any brand stay hidden, which is what the note was protecting. His ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop; noted only.

v02 fixes the v01 faults. The church on the hill is gone, and the distant houses are low tiled houses half hidden in palms. The kneeling official is now behind the chavers at the far right, hands raised. There is clear ground between the chavers and the horses, so no contact yet. The camera is low at the waterline with reflections. Nagoji leads on the grey with his talwar raised; his moustache and clean chin match the sheet. The lancers wear white turbans on dark horses, and the Maravar riders behind them are bare-headed. The chavers are bare-chested and ash-smeared, with topknots, swords and round shields. Open sky at the top left and right takes the two captions. Minor note: the official is partly cut off by the right edge. His ear ornament is a small drop; noted only.

v02 fixes the v01 faults: the hilltop fort is gone and the border line is removed. It keeps the dusk village road with thatched and tiled houses. A riderless dark-brown charger with an empty quilted saddle walks in the column. The bandages are clean white on the forearms, and one lancer's arm is in a cloth sling; there is no blood. Nagoji leads on the grey, grave and looking straight ahead. He is in the foreground, ahead of everyone, though not quite a full horse-length clear. The white-turbaned lancers and the bare-headed Maravar riders behind him look toward his back. A band of clear dusk sky across the top (y 0 to 0.2, mostly on the left) takes both captions. Minor notes: the Maravar riders are bare-chested with shoulder cloths rather than in short jackets, and the riderless horse's lead rein is not clearly held. His ear ornament is a small drop; noted only.

v02 fixes the v01 faults: the fort is gone, and the verandah is now a Kerala palace verandah with a laterite plinth, dark carved wooden pillars, eaves of curved clay tiles and a carved wooden screen window. Nagoji's chin and jaw are clean-shaven with no stubble or mole, and his sleeves are down to the wrists, so no forearm mark shows. Ramayyan matches his sheet: thin, fine features, receding curly hair, plain white cloth. He sits cross-legged on the high plinth, his head nearly level with Nagoji's, writing on a blank palm-leaf bundle with his eyes down. The brass lamp has open wicks. The white-turbaned column files past behind on dark horses. Open sky in the upper middle (x 0.36 to 0.58, y 0.02 to 0.22) takes Ramayyan's balloon, with a short tail to his mouth. His ear ornament is a small hanging drop; noted only. v01 is not acceptable because of the fort and the classical stone columns.

Clean on the beat. The open dark-wood pavilion sits beside the temple wall, with a bare copper flagmast and tiered roofs in the background. Nagoji steps up barefoot with his boots at the step and a blank ola in hand. He is in the commander look with talwar, curled moustache and clean chin. His left arm's inner side is turned away, so no brand shows. Ramayyan matches his sheet and sits cross-legged at the low desk, writing without looking up, with blank bundles at his knee. There is no lamp and no ritual object. Note only: the ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop, not a stud. Minor: the art has a thin painted black border about 15 to 18 px inside the edge, with a white margin outside it; trim about 20 px per side before placement. Lettering: the caption fits in the sky above and left of Nagoji's turban. Ramayyan's balloon fits in the sky at upper right above the temple roofs, or on the dark wooden back panel left of his head.

v02 is clean. The edit removed the mottled patch from Nagoji's left forearm, and both forearms are now plain skin. Everything else is kept from v01: the same open dark oiled-wood pavilion with the laterite temple wall, clay-tiled temple roof and palms (it matches 2.1). Nagoji is barefoot with arms crossed in the commander look (rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, talwar) with a thick curled moustache and a clean chin. Ramayyan matches his sheet and sits cross-legged at the low desk in three-quarter view, writing on a blank leaf, with blank bundles at his knee. There is no lamp and no ritual object, no painted text and no border. Hands and feet are sound. Note only: Nagoji's ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop, not a stud. Lettering: Nagoji's balloon goes in the sky right of his head (about x 0.35 to 0.55, y 0.15 to 0.30). Ramayyan's balloon goes in the upper-right sky (about x 0.60 to 0.92, y 0.12 to 0.32). The caption goes along the top beam or the upper sky. v01 is still unacceptable because of the forearm patch.

v02 is clean. The setting is fixed to the dark oiled-wood pavilion with the grey laterite temple wall, palms and clay-tiled temple roofs, with no water and no distant house. The lamp and brass vessel are gone, so the only props are the desk, blank palm-leaf bundles and the stylus. Ramayyan matches his sheet: receding hair, curly black sides, clean-shaven, thin sharp features, plain white cloth. He has raised his head and glances up and slightly toward frame left, toward where Nagoji stands in 2.2, and the stylus is paused just above a blank leaf. The only marks on the leaf are its two binding holes, with no writing. The writing hand is sound. There is no painted text or border. Lettering: plain dark wood above and on both sides of his head. The caption goes upper left (about x 0.02 to 0.30, y 0.03 to 0.25). The two Ramayyan balloons go upper right (about x 0.62 to 0.95, y 0.03 to 0.30) and across the top centre. v01 is still unacceptable (lit brass lamp, backwater background).

v02 is clean. There is no fort, sea, boats or European houses. Behind him are the dark pavilion pillars and beams, the grey laterite temple wall, clay-tiled temple roofs and palms under open sky, consistent with 2.1 to 2.3. The shot is from below with the chin raised. He faces frame right toward the seated minister, with a level, proud gaze. Commander look intact: rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, talwar. He has the thick curled moustache, a cleanly shaved chin with no stubble, and a small gold ball stud on the lobe. His sleeves fall to the wrists, so no forearm marks show. The hands at the bottom edge are sound. There is no painted text or border. Lettering: the large upper-right sky (about x 0.47 to 0.90, y 0.12 to 0.45) takes both Nagoji balloons. The caption fits the upper-left sky (about x 0.08 to 0.28, y 0.03 to 0.20) or along the top beam. v01 is still unacceptable (hilltop fort, bay with sails, stubble, forearm patch).

v02 is clean. The setting is now the dark oiled-wood pavilion (dark pillars and back panel) with the laterite temple wall, clay-tiled temple roofs and palms beyond. The whitewashed wall, lamp and brass pot are all gone. Ramayyan matches his sheet: receding hair, curly black sides, clean-shaven, thin features, plain white cloth. His eyes are down, finished with the matter. The stylus point rests in one faint pale groove on an otherwise blank leaf, which has only binding holes. The camera is tighter on the hand and stylus than in v01, with his face beyond it. Both hands are sound: a pen grip seen from the back of the hand, and four fingertips resting on the leaf. There is no painted text or border. Lettering: the upper-left sky (about x 0.10 to 0.32, y 0.02 to 0.22) and upper-right sky (about x 0.70 to 0.95, y 0.02 to 0.20) take the two Ramayyan balloons. v01 is still unacceptable (lamp, brass pot, whitewashed wall).

v02 fixes the v01 fault: Nagoji's lost profile now shows the thick curled moustache and a clean-shaven chin and jaw. Every horse in the stable is brown, so the grey gelding is the only grey. The rest matches the beat: approach road under palms, tiered dark clay-tile house, compound wall with two tuskers in its shade, long stable at right, Nagoji (rust-red turban, red sash, cream tunic, boots, talwar) and Ibrahim (white turban, grey-flecked beard, teal short coat, brown pony) small in the left foreground. The open sky across the upper middle takes both captions. Minor notes: the stable has a squared-off straw bundle, which is small background detail and not disqualifying. At this scale his ear ornament cannot be read (note only). v01 is rejected for a bearded chin.

v02 removes the woman with the lamp plate. The background guards are now bare-chested Nair spearmen in white mundu with no turbans, which matches 3.3. The woven frond and mango-leaf arch has hanging brass lamps with open wicks and thin smoke. Nagoji is on the grey gelding with a clean-shaven chin, moustache, rust-red turban, sash and talwar. Ibrahim is on the brown horse, turned and gesturing toward Nagoji. His scar runs from the ear toward the jaw on his LEFT cheek. Hands are sound. The open sky between and above the two turbans takes both balloons. Notes only: Nagoji's ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop rather than a stud, which the author has not decided. Ibrahim's scar is a reddish line, as on his sheet, and does not read as blood. His mount is horse-sized rather than a small pony. v01 is rejected for the woman in frame.

Clean. The thick-walled granary has its doors open on high mounds of paddy. Three bare-chested Nair spearmen in white mundu stand at ease in the shade of a pillared, tile-roofed inner verandah, away from the gate. There are no principals, no text and no anachronism, and the architecture matches 3.1. Minor: the stacked sacks look a little like modern gunny sacks, but this is acceptable.

v02 is in the book's inked, painted style, not photographic. It shows the same limewashed granary wall on a grey stone plinth as the chosen 3.3 frame, with beaten-earth ground and scattered paddy husks. One low, plain wooden panel is set into the wall base, with no handle, latch, hinge, carving or writing. Its frame edges are worn darker and glossier than the paler board in the middle. The plain upper wall gives ample low-detail space for both captions. Minor: the panel sits in mixed light under a diagonal sun band rather than full shadow, and a few tiny nail heads show on the board. Neither is disqualifying. v01 is rejected for its photographic style and an all-timber wall that does not match the granary.

Minor: Nagoji and Ibrahim are still mounted rather than visibly swinging down, though Nagoji's lean reads as the start of a dismount and the arrival beat and caption still work. The well's pulley rope ends in an iron ring, not a noose. The courtyard floor is packed earth here but stone paving in 4.2. Everything else is clean: the women wear off-white mundu with the upper cloth over one shoulder, no blouse, no blue, bangles only; the boys with short spears and the older man correcting one are at the well; every head turns to the gate; Nagoji has his rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, boots, talwar, clean chin and gold ear drop on the only grey horse; Ibrahim has his white turban, grey-flecked beard and teal short coat on a brown mount; the hanging lamp is open brass. Clear sky at top centre for the caption.

Minor continuity: the courtyard is stone-paved and empty, and its right side is a plain whitewashed compound wall, so it does not quite match 4.1's sandy courtyard with the well and the women on mats (the script only requires no one in the foreground). Padmini matches her sheet: thick black hair coiled at the nape, gold at ears and throat, cream gold-bordered sari in the old drape over one shoulder with no blouse, hitched above bare ankles, hand on a long stick, alone at the far end. The tail for Ibrahim (off-panel, beside the viewer at the gate) is set on the bottom edge. A large clear sky gives room for both lettering areas.

v02 is clean. It is the right estate courtyard: packed sandy earth, a carved dark-oiled pillared verandah under curved clay tiles, whitewashed walls and coconut palms, with no fort, sea, soldiers or barrels. That matches 4.1. Nagoji is in his commander look: rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, cream trousers, talwar, and brown riding boots clearly shown. He has the thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin and a small gold ear drop (noted only, not a fault). His right hand is on his chest and his head is inclined in a shallow bow. His sleeves are down, so no brand shows. Ibrahim is frame-right with a white turban, grey-flecked beard, teal short coat over the pocketed vest, and the pale scar on his LEFT cheek (frame-right side of his face), presenting with open palms. Hands and anatomy are sound, and there is no text. The only lamp is an open brass standing lamp on the verandah. The framing is full-length rather than a mid-shot, which the round 1 correction asked for so the boots show. Clear sky across the upper part of the frame holds the caption (upper left) and Ibrahim's balloon (above him) without touching faces. v01 stays rejected: fort, sea, Portuguese soldiers, and the brand showing early.

v01 is a waist-up portrait with Nagoji's whole face, not the script's insert of his left hand at his belt ('where her eyes go'). The background is a Deccan hill fort, rocky hills and stone ramparts, not the Kerala estate courtyard. Nagoji's chin carries visible stubble, against the clean-shaven rule. The ridged nails are not legible. The brand patch on the left forearm is plausible (pale ridges, no letters), but the rest of the frame fails.
decisions.correction: FRAMING AND SETTING CORRECTION: This is a tight insert close-up, NOT a portrait. No face, no head, no turban and no shoulders in frame. Show only Nagoji's left side at the waist: the broad red sash and the edge of the cream tunic, and his LEFT hand resting on a worn leather belt whose leather has rubbed pale. His thumb is hooked over the belt, which turns the inner side of the forearm slightly toward the viewer. The fingernails are healed but visibly ridged and uneven. The cream sleeve cuff has ridden up a little, and just below its edge, on the inner left forearm a hand's width above the wrist, the lower edge of the Portuguese brand shows: a pale puckered patch of raised scar ridges, blurred and unreadable, with no letters, numerals, cross or tattoo-like lines. The brass talwar hilt may show at the frame edge. The background is a soft, out-of-focus Kerala estate courtyard (sandy earth, a dark oiled wooden pillar, whitewashed wall, curved clay roof tiles) in the same warm midday light as the neighbouring panels. NO hill fort, no Deccan hills, no stone ramparts, no open landscape. No text or lettering space is needed.

decisions.issues: v02 is clean and matches her sheet. Her hair is thick and black (light highlights only, no grey), drawn back and coiled in a low bun at the nape. She has gold ball ear studs, a plain gold neck ring and a gold bangle, and a cream cotton sari with a gold border in the old Kerala drape over one shoulder, with no stitched blouse. She stands, one hand resting on top of her long walking stick, and the hand is sound. Her face is unhurried, turned slightly frame-right toward Nagoji off panel. There is no second figure. The setting is the estate courtyard: a dark carved pillar, a whitewashed wall under clay tiles, coconut palms, an open brass pot, midday light. Both her balloons fit in the clear sky upper centre, between her head and the roof at right. There is no text in the art. A small note: the neck ring is a smooth torque rather than the sheet's beaded chain, which still reads as simple gold. v01 stays rejected for loose grey hair, a seated pose, and the bearded rag-clad over-the-shoulder figure.

Acceptable. The face matches the sheet: thick curled moustache, rust-red turban, cream collar with the red sash at the shoulder, and a small gold bead stud (correct). The chin and jaw carry faint stubble-like shading. It reads as shadow and there is no beard, so it is within tolerance, but note it. The framing is a little wider than the script's turban edge to chin: the whole turban and the neck are visible. The plain plastered wall on the left half gives ample clean space for both Nagoji lines.

v02 is clean. It is a close shot of Padmini Amma with a wry one-sided smile. Her hair is glossy black in a nape coil with no grey. She wears gold ball earrings, a gold bead necklace and a cream sari with a plain gold-stripe border and no blouse, and her right hand grips the long stick firmly. She stands in the Nair estate courtyard: whitewashed wall with clay-tile coping, a dark oiled wooden pillar, tiled eaves and palms. There is no waterfront or boat, and the image is full-bleed. The sky at upper right is clear for the balloon. v01 is rejected: it has a waterfront with a sea wall and sailing boat, grey-streaked hair and a painted white margin.

v02 is acceptable. The courtyard and gatehouse match the estate: whitewashed walls with clay-tile coping, plain wooden gate doors, palms and a packed-earth floor. There is no fort or arched stone gate. Nagoji is in the full commander look, still booted (correct before 5.4), with a curled moustache and clean chin. The grey gelding has a quilted saddle and a plain bridle, and all four legs read correctly. A bare-chested boy in a white mundu leads it. Padmini's off-panel hand grips the stick firmly over a plain gold-striped cream border. The sky at upper centre and right is clear. Minor: Nagoji lets go with his LEFT hand rather than the right the prompt asked for, but both rolled forearms are unmarked, so no brand shows. Note only: his ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop. v01 is rejected for the hilltop fort and the ashlar fortress wall and gate.

v02 is acceptable. The shaded verandah has dark oiled carved pillars, wooden beams, a polished stone floor and a whitewashed wall. Padmini is on the left, half a step ahead. Her hair is black, her stick tip rests on the stone, and she wears no blouse. Nagoji walks barefoot beside her, sleeves down to the wrists and no marks on his arms, with a clean chin and curled moustache. His brown boots stand at the verandah step by the pillar. Out in the sunlit courtyard, Ibrahim (white turban, grey-flecked beard, teal short coat over a pocketed vest) talks with a steward. Porters carry sacks near the granary under clay-tile roofs and palms. The brass lamp with open wicks stands on a low plinth. There is no framed picture and no European table. The pale wall above and left of Padmini's head is clear for both balloons. Notes: Ibrahim's left-cheek scar is too small to read at this scale, though nothing appears on his right cheek. The polished floor is very reflective, but it reads as polished, not wet. Nagoji's ear ornament is a small drop (note only). v01 is rejected: grey at Padmini's temples, a framed picture on the wall and a turned-leg table.

v02 is acceptable. It is a two-shot on a verandah of the same build as 5.4: dark wooden beams, plain stone pillars, a polished stone floor and a whitewashed wall. Padmini strides right in profile, eyes forward, with her stick in one hand and her other hand lifting her gold-striped cream sari; no blouse. Nagoji walks barefoot a step behind, sleeves down with no marks, chin clean and moustache curled. Beyond are clay-tile roofs, a slatted granary, a fruiting jackfruit tree and palms. There is no fort. A large clear sky across the upper right half takes all three balloons: Nagoji's at the left end of the sky or over the dark beams, Padmini's two to the right. Hands and feet are sound. Minor notes: the image has a thin painted black edge line about 3 px wide on all four sides, so trim it or let the panel border cover it. Padmini's hair has grey-toned gloss highlights near the crown and temple; they read as sheen on black hair and match 5.4, but watch this across the page. A plain wooden stand with a brass lamp and a brass pot sits cut off at the left edge. It is not obviously European, but it is a borderline furniture item. Nagoji's ear ornament is a small drop (note only). v01 is rejected: the hilltop fort, a visible mark on Nagoji's forearm, grey hair at Padmini's temple and heavy carved temple-granite pillars.

Clean. Padmini's hair is now glossy black, coiled at the nape, with no grey. Everything else from v01 is kept: Nagoji seen from behind (rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, face hidden), the two young women in plain off-white cloth tying blank palm-leaf bundles (one glancing up), and Padmini in near profile with her eyes sliding toward him. The lamp is an open brass nilavilakku and the window has wooden bars. The caption fits on the plain grey wall band at the top, between the turban and the window (x 0.30 to 0.55, y 0 to 0.17). Note only: Nagoji's ear ornament is a small gold ball, not a flat stud. v01 was rejected for grey hair.

Acceptable. Her hair is now solid black with no grey. Padmini is in profile at the left edge, pointing her stick into a dim room. The room has an iron-strapped wooden chest, an arched niche with a small unlit open brass lamp, a rolled mat against the wall and a wooden-barred window. There is a large plain wall in the upper centre for the balloon. Minor: the stick shows only about one and a half forearm-lengths, because its far end is hidden in her fist, so it reads a little short for a long walking stick, but the pointing beat is clear. v01 was rejected for grey hair.

Acceptable. All three corrections landed. Her hair is jet-black. The room behind her through the dark doorframe matches 6.2: iron-strapped chest, arched lamp niche, rolled mat and barred window. There are no chairs and no European furniture. Nagoji's shoulder, cream tunic, red sash, rust-red turban and curly hair sit at the left edge with his face turned away, and the visible jaw is clean-shaven apart from faint shading. Two plain wall areas are clear for the balloons: x 0.30 to 0.50 by y 0.03 to 0.22, and x 0.62 to 0.95 by y 0.04 to 0.17. Minor continuity point: the niche lamp is lit here but unlit in 6.2. Note only: his ear ornament is a small gold ball. v01 was rejected for grey hair, the garden doorway and the furniture.

Acceptable. The hilltop fort and the chair are gone. The background is now the Nair estate: low tiered roofs of curved clay tiles, a pillared verandah, coconut palms and a jackfruit tree with fruit. Nagoji matches the commander sheet: rust-red turban, thick curled moustache, clean chin, cream tunic with sleeves to the wrist (no brand showing), red sash, sheathed talwar. He is barefoot on the verandah with a confident lean, and his hands and feet are sound. There is open sky at the upper right for the balloon. Minor: a very faint, low blue hill shows behind the palms near the roofline, with no fort or structure on it. Note only: his ear ornament is a small gold drop. v01 was rejected for the fort and the chair.

v01 (the only candidate) has a low horizontal angle along a polished verandah floor, carved pillars on stone bases, a courtyard of clay-tile roofs and palms, and Padmini Amma's stern face in the right third with open sky for the balloon. The staging, though, is broken. (1) There are two walking sticks and, in effect, two people: the left foreground shows a ferrule-tipped stick beside a separate figure's gold-bordered sari hem and bare foot, while Padmini Amma at the right holds a second stick in her hand. (2) Padmini Amma's figure has a hard cut-out outline and sits pasted against the background, cut off at the floor edge as if behind a ledge rather than standing on the verandah. (3) Her hair shows grey streaks at the temple, which breaks the thick BLACK hair, not-grey-yet rule.
decisions.correction: Keep the low camera close to the polished dark verandah floor, the horizontal composition, the row of carved wooden pillars on stone bases receding at the left, the courtyard behind with low tiered clay-tile roofs and coconut palms, the open sky at the upper centre for the balloon, and Padmini Amma's stern face and shoulders in the right third, turned full toward the viewer's left. Fix the staging. There is exactly ONE person and exactly ONE walking stick in the frame. Remove the extra sari hem and bare foot from the left foreground. Padmini Amma, standing on the verandah floor in the right third, holds her single long walking stick in her right hand and thrusts it out at an angle, so that its iron-shod tip strikes the polished floor in the left foreground close to the camera. The shaft runs as one continuous straight line from her hand to the tip, and she holds no other stick. Draw her standing on the same floor in the same warm light as the setting, with no cut-out outline around her body and her lower body continuing naturally to the floor. Her hair is thick, glossy and jet-black all through, coiled at the nape, with NO grey, silver or white strands anywhere. She wears the cream sari with a gold border in the old Kerala drape with no stitched blouse, with gold at her ears and throat.

decisions.issues: Clean pick. The fort from v01 is gone: the background now shows only palms, trees, a tiled kalari pavilion and estate roofs. Padmini's hair is fully black. Notes only: (1) Nagoji's ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop, not a stud. (2) His sleeves are rolled up here, so the brand shows on his LEFT forearm as a pale puckered patch with no letters, sitting about mid-forearm. This fits the bible's 'seen when sleeves are pushed up', but in 7.2 to 7.4 his sleeves are down. (3) The kalari youths show from the waist up behind the low wall, not just heads. The girl wears a white chest wrap. v01 is not acceptable because of the crenellated fort wall behind the kalari.

Only candidate v01 is set in the wrong place: a stone pillared mandapam with stone steps, with no jackfruit tree and no round platform, so it breaks continuity with 7.1's courtyard. Padmini Amma's hair is heavily grey-streaked and loose, not black and coiled at the nape. Nagoji's brand is a reddish rash-like blotch near the ELBOW of his outstretched left forearm instead of a pale puckered patch a hand's width above the wrist. The young woman hands him the tumbler instead of setting tumblers down. These parts work: the women's plain off-white mundu and upper cloth (no blouse, no blue, no border), the second woman with a plate of fruit and snacks, Nagoji barefoot and clean-shaven, and open sky upper left for the two captions. Note only: his ear ornament is a hanging drop.
decisions.correction: Set this in the same small inner courtyard as panel 7.1. Nagoji and Padmini Amma sit side by side on the round, worn stone platform at the foot of the huge jackfruit tree, with its thick trunk, a few hanging jackfruits and dappled leaf shade, and the low laterite courtyard wall and curved clay-tile roofs behind. There is NO stone pillared hall, NO carved stone columns, NO mandapam steps and no fort anywhere. Padmini Amma's hair is thick jet-black, coiled neatly at the nape, with no grey or silver at all. The first young woman bends to set two brass tumblers of water down on the platform beside them, unhurried, her eyes meeting Nagoji's. Keep the second young woman behind her carrying a plate of sliced fruit and fried snacks, both women in plain off-white mundu with an upper cloth over one shoulder exactly as drawn. Nagoji's sleeves are down to the wrist so no forearm mark shows. Keep clear sky or leaf shade in the upper left for two captions.

decisions.issues: Clean pick. The setting matches 7.1: jackfruit trunk, worn round platform and Kerala tiled houses with wooden-barred windows, with no fort and no stone pavilion. Padmini has black hair, the gold-bordered sari with no blouse, a gold necklace and earrings, and she bites a golden jackfruit bulb with juice on her fingers and a cloth in her other hand. Nagoji is barefoot with his sleeves down and a level look. Open sky across the top takes the three balloons. Notes only: Nagoji's ear ornament is a small hanging drop. Padmini's cloth has thin gold stripes rather than being plain. v01 is not acceptable: it shows a hilltop fort and a stone pillar, and Padmini has grey hair.

Clean pick. Nagoji is in a close shot, off-centre low on the left, against the jackfruit trunk, with an unguarded, faraway upward look. His rust-red turban is fully wrapped, and he has the cream tunic and red sash, a thick curled moustache, a clean chin with faint shading and a small gold stud on the lobe. There are no boots, no forearm mark, no fields and no fort. The laterite wall and Kerala tiled roofs carry on from 7.1. Pale sky at upper right and the trunk area at upper left give room for four lettering items. PADMINI (off) is placed at the left edge because she sits to his left in 7.3. v01 is not acceptable: it shows a hilltop fort and paddy fields, Nagoji is bare-headed and he wears boots.

Acceptable. Padmini Amma is alone, filling the canvas edge to edge, seated on the platform under the jackfruit tree with the laterite wall and a tiled roof behind. She wipes her fingers on a small cloth, glances toward screen right (where Nagoji sits in 7.3) and looks faintly amused. Her costume matches her sheet: gold-bordered sari with no blouse, bead necklace, earrings, bangles and the stick beside her. Sky at upper right takes the one balloon. Notes only: her black hair carries blue-grey glossy highlights that read as sheen, not grey. The hair is worn loose and full at the neck rather than in a visible coil. The cloth has thin gold stripes. The frame is portrait (1024x1536), so it needs cropping for the small bottom-right inset. v01 is not acceptable: it includes a bearded man seen over the shoulder, and Padmini has grey streaks in her hair.

v02 is acceptable. v01 (only candidate): the script beat is wrong. Nagoji stands on a rocky hillside against a generic tree, not in the estate courtyard by the jackfruit tree. The memory is not a desaturated stain bleeding in behind his head. It is painted as a full-colour, real dawn landscape that continues straight from where he stands, so he seems to be watching a live Maratha column charge a coastal fort from Kerala. The riders are mid-sized rather than small and distant, and their white headwear reads as rounded helmets or caps rather than wrapped pagdis. A puckered brand-like patch shows on his left forearm near the elbow, not a hand's width above the wrist, and the prompt does not call for it here. Light stubble on the chin. His ear ornament is a hanging drop (noted only). What works: his face and costume, the plain saffron swallow-tailed pennant, the whitewashed fort with low bastions and no flag, white angarkhas, and no text.
decisions.correction: Keep Nagoji in the present, in full warm colour, in Padmini Amma's inner courtyard. He sits on the stone platform with his shoulder against the trunk of the jackfruit tree (glossy leaves, green jackfruits on the trunk), with the clay-tiled roofs of the Nair house behind him. He gazes out of frame to the north, and he is NOT looking at a real landscape. The memory is a faded, desaturated sepia-grey wash that seeps in behind his head from the upper-right panel edge like a watercolour stain, with soft, dissolving, ragged edges and no border. Inside it, a column of tiny, distant Maratha riders in white angarkhas and soft, white, wrapped cloth pagdis (not helmets or round caps) rides at dawn under one plain saffron swallow-tailed pennant toward a low whitewashed fort wall with low bastions, which flies no flag. Keep his face with the thick curled moustache and a smooth, CLEAN-SHAVEN chin with no stubble, plus his rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash and talwar. Keep both sleeves down, or turn his left forearm away, so no mark shows. Keep the upper part of the stain pale and low in detail for two lettering areas.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. No jackfruit tree is drawn in frame, though a basket of bulbs and leaf shade are present.

Acceptable. It is a wide, high view down into the courtyard. Nagoji is barefoot on the platform, head back in a laugh, with turban, tunic, sash and talwar. Crows burst from a fruiting jackfruit tree and stay to the left side. Padmini sits beside him, unmoved, with her stick. A woman in a plain off-white drape over one shoulder, with no blouse and no gold border, turns in the far doorway. The lamp is an open brass lamp. The upper-centre courtyard floor is plain for both balloons. Notes: Nagoji's ear ornament is a small hanging drop (noted only). A small pinkish puckered patch shows on his left forearm closer to the elbow than a hand's width above the wrist; it reads as a scar, with no letters or cross. Padmini's hair carries some grey streaks.

v02 is clean. The setting is now the estate courtyard (clay-tiled roofs, carved wooden pillars, whitewashed walls, coconut palms) with no hill or fort. Padmini's hair is black. v02 is acceptable. The setting is the estate courtyard (whitewashed wall, tiled roofs, wooden pillars, palms) with no hill, fort or water. Only candidate v01. Padmini's close-up is good: she leans in with a toothy smile and holds her stick, and there is open sky for one balloon. It fails on three counts. (1) A man is seen from behind in the right foreground, and he is not Nagoji: he has a full black BEARD, no rust-red turban, and a dark coat with a leather shoulder strap and a brass stud. He reads as a stranger, or as Nagoji wrongly bearded and wrongly dressed, in a panel whose cast is Padmini alone. (2) The setting is a waterfront, with open sea, an island, stacked baskets, sacks and a jetty wall, not the jackfruit-tree platform in the estate's inner courtyard. (3) Padmini's hair has grey streaks at the front and temple; the bible wants thick BLACK hair, not grey yet.
decisions.correction: Keep Padmini exactly as drawn: close on her as she leans forward with a broad, teeth-showing smile, holding her long dark wooden walking stick, in a cream sari of the old Kerala drape with no blouse and simple gold at her ears and throat, with open space upper right for one balloon. Her thick hair is jet BLACK all over, coiled at the nape, with not one grey or silver streak. Set her on the stone platform under the jackfruit tree in the enclosed inner courtyard of her Nair estate: whitewashed wall, carved oiled wooden pillar, clay-tiled eaves, jackfruit leaves, and sky above the low courtyard wall. There must be NO sea, river, harbour, island, jetty, sacks or baskets. Draw no other person, or at most a narrow sliver of Nagoji's shoulder at the right edge in his cream tunic with the broad red sash and the edge of his rust-red turban. NEVER a bearded man, a dark coat, a leather strap or a brass stud.

decisions.issues: v02 is acceptable. The fort and the stone temple columns are gone; the courtyard now has carved wooden pillars, tiled roofs, whitewashed walls, the jackfruit tree and palms. Deviation from the correction: the extended arm is still his LEFT arm with the sleeve pushed up, so the inner left forearm is bare and unmarked. Note only: his ear ornament is a hanging drop. v01 is rejected: it has the hilltop fort, stone temple columns, grey in Padmini's hair and a visible forearm mark.

The background shows a large European-style coastal fort with stone bastions and domed sentry turrets across open sea. It also has a whitewashed European-looking building. The chapter is set on an inland Nair estate with paddy beyond, and forts and European buildings are forbidden unless the prompt names them. The steward holds a European-style wooden writing board or ledger, which is an anachronism. It should be a blank palm-leaf bundle or nothing. Nagoji shows a light stubble shadow on his chin. Ibrahim (white turban, grey-flecked beard, teal short coat, pocketed vest), the ox cart, the riders unloading saddlebags and Nagoji's unsmiling sideways look are all good.
decisions.correction: The outer yard belongs to Padmini Amma's inland Nair estate in Travancore. Show no fort, bastion, sentry turret, battlement, harbour, sea or whitewashed European building anywhere. Behind the yard show low tiered roofs of curved country clay tiles on carved oiled wooden posts, a laterite compound wall, a raised granary, coconut palms and green paddy beyond, with open sky above. The steward is an estate man in a plain white mundu with a shoulder cloth. He holds a blank palm-leaf bundle tied with string, with no marks on it, or nothing at all, never a book, board or ledger. Keep everything else that worked: Nagoji framed in the shadowed passage at left, unsmiling, his eyes turned toward the yard, with a smooth clean-shaven chin and no stubble; Ibrahim in his white turban, short grey-flecked beard, teal short coat and pocketed vest standing beside the ox cart; the two riders of the column unloading saddlebags; and clear sky in the upper part of the frame for the three lettering areas.

decisions.issues: Padmini Amma is drawn STANDING against the trunk. In 10.1 and 10.5 she is seated against the trunk and on the stone platform, so this breaks continuity within the page. Her hair shows visible grey-silver streaks at the front and crown, but the chapter requires black hair that is not grey yet. The background switches to a backwater lagoon with a sailing boat, which contradicts the green paddy beyond the wall in 10.1. Boats are also not named in the prompt. Her face, the amused half-smile and the sari drape are good.
decisions.correction: Padmini Amma is SEATED, not standing. She sits on the low laterite stone platform at the foot of the jackfruit tree (green leaves and hanging jackfruit above) and eases her back against the trunk, legs folded under her cream gold-bordered sari in the old Kerala drape with no blouse. Her long walking stick rests against her shoulder or across her lap. Keep the faint, almost amused half-smile and sidelong look that worked in this frame. Her hair is thick and entirely jet-black, with no grey or silver strands, coiled at the nape. Behind her, match the previous panels: the estate courtyard's low laterite wall with green paddy fields and coconut palms beyond. Show no lagoon, backwater, river, sea, boat or sail. She is the only person in frame. Keep the open pale sky in the upper part of the frame for the three lettering areas.

decisions.issues: A large hilltop fort with towers and battlements dominates the right background. Padmini Amma's hair is heavily grey, with a silver-grey crown and streaks, but the chapter requires black hair that is not grey yet. The staging is good: the two-shot on the stone platform under the jackfruit tree, Nagoji barefoot with his talwar against the trunk, and Padmini laying her stick across her knees.
decisions.correction: Remove the hilltop fort entirely. Behind the pair show only the estate's laterite compound wall, coconut palms, green paddy and open sky, with no fort, castle, ruin, tower or battlement on any hill or horizon. Padmini Amma's hair is thick and entirely jet-black, with no grey, silver or white strands anywhere, coiled at the nape. If Nagoji's brand is visible, it sits on the inner side of his LEFT forearm a hand's width above the wrist (not near the elbow): a small pale puckered patch of raised ridges with no letters. Otherwise keep that forearm turned so the brand is hidden. Nagoji's chin and jaw are cleanly shaven, with no stubble. Keep everything else that worked: the two-shot on the stone platform under the jackfruit tree; Nagoji barefoot in his rust-red turban, cream tunic and red sash, with his talwar leaning against the trunk; Padmini laying her stick across her knees with a subtle shift in her expression; and the wide clear sky above for the three lettering areas.

decisions.issues: v02 is clean and fixes everything wrong with v01. Padmini Amma sits in full colour on the low stone platform under the jackfruit tree, with the estate's clay-tile roof and carved verandah behind her. Her thick hair is black with no grey, and she wears gold studs, a bead necklace and bangles, a cream Kerala drape with no blouse, and holds her long stick. Her hands are sound. She looks to the right at the off-panel listener, so the NAGOJI (off) tail points to the top of the right edge, above Varma's crest. The memory of Varma fills the right half in a faded sepia wash that dissolves into the foliage, with no border. He wears his court look: the cream-and-gold turban with the jewelled peacock crest, Vaishnavite namam, bare chest, gold-bordered shoulder cloth, pearl and gold necklaces and chin on hand. A spear stands at his shoulder and a sheathed sword lies within reach. The plain map shows only faint lines and has no writing. The map lies on his low wooden platform rather than on a mat, which is a minor point. There is no guard, sea, fort or text. Lettering fits in the pale upper middle and the washed-out top right, with the caption over the top-left leaves. v01 stays rejected: wrong setting (the king's seaside hall), the memory in full colour, and grey in Padmini's hair.

Clean. Only Padmini Amma is in frame. She holds the stick upright before her, with a dark jackfruit tree and its fruit behind her, palms and an estate clay-tile roof at the lower right. Acceptable. v02 is acceptable and fixes v01's setting. The scene is now the courtyard of the Nair estate. The jackfruit tree's dark trunk, leaves and hanging fruit are behind Nagoji. Behind Padmini are a laterite wall, low tiered clay-tile roofs on carved dark pillars, an open brass standing lamp, potted plants, coconut palms and open sky. There is no fort, ruin or text. Nagoji sits on the stone edge of the platform in his commander look: rust-red turban, cream tunic with sleeves pushed up, red sash and cream trousers. He is barefoot, with both bare feet large in the foreground (five toes each, sound), and looks up after her. His hands are sound, his sheathed talwar leans beside him with a brass hilt like the sheet's, and his forearms show no marks. Padmini walks away barefoot with her long stick and looks back over her shoulder. Her hair is black, she wears a gold stud and necklace, and her cream drape leaves her back bare with no blouse. Minor notes: Nagoji's ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop, noted only. A light stubble shadow on his chin and jaw matches the accepted 11.3 frame and still reads as clean-shaven, with no beard. Open sky in the upper centre and upper right takes both of Padmini's lines clear of both faces. v01 stays rejected for the hilltop forts and the ruined-citadel setting.

Acceptable with notes. Padmini Amma matches her sheet, seen from behind as she walks away down the middle of the courtyard: thick black hair coiled at the nape (one faint grey strand at the temple, as on the sheet), gold ear studs and necklace, a cream gold-bordered sari in the old drape with no stitched blouse, barefoot, and her long stick in her right hand. The women of the house stand aside along the verandah steps with heads bowed. They wear plain off-white cloth with an upper cloth, no blouse, no blue and no coin necklace. Bare-chested men with topknots sit at their palm-leaf bundles, which carry no visible writing. The firewood girl at the right edge looks back, bright-eyed. The estate is right: tiled roofs, carved dark pillars, the jackfruit tree at upper right, brass pots, and no Europeans, forts or glass. No lettering is needed. Four things to fix before placement: (1) The carved frieze on the far beam above Padmini's head (about x 0.29 to 0.39, y 0.225 to 0.24) has faint Latin-like letter shapes, roughly 'GOMEAN'. They are about 10 px tall and under 1 mm in print, so they read as carving at page size. Clone or blur that band into plain moulding; the lintel over the central door has a fainter version of the same at about x 0.30 to 0.37, y 0.29. (2) A small framed plaque hangs on the right verandah wall (about x 0.69, y 0.29). It could read as a hung picture; minor. (3) A mustard-yellow underlayer shows under the firewood girl's upper cloth at her shoulder (about x 0.95, y 0.48). It could read as a stitched blouse; minor and small. (4) The girl looks left toward the courtyard rather than clearly back at the jackfruit tree behind her; acceptable.
